animalProducts.title: Izinkukhu: Laying hens (commercial)
lines: Izakhiwo ezikhona ezingu-1; ezihlongozwayo ezingu-0. Uhlobo lokukhiqiza olukhethiwe: amaqanda. Akucatshangwa isibalo sezilwane noma okukhiqizwayo.
Iseluleko sokuthenga: ukukhiqiza amaqanda, cela izikhukhukazi ezincane ezigonyiwe esezizozalela kumhlinzeki wezinkukhu ezizalelayo, namarekhodi eminyaka, ukudla nokugonywa.

Hlela ukudla okunomsoco olinganiselwe, amanzi ahlanzekile, umthunzi, umoya nokuvikelwa ezilwaneni ezidlayo. Ukutholakala kwamaqanda kuncike ezinkukhwini ezizalelayo, ubudala bazo, impilo nokunakekelwa; ihhoko lodwa alinikezi amaqanda.
Qoqa amaqanda njalo, ugcine okwandlalwe ezidlekeni kuhlanzekile futhi komile, uphathe/ugcine amaqanda ngokucophelela ukuze asetshenziswe ekhaya noma athengiswe.

Inkomba yesikhathi: With a constant 14–16 hour light day, commercial hens keep laying at a high rate all year. Le nkomba yokuphatha kwezohwebo ayisho ukutholakala kwamaqanda kwasekhaya okulinganayo ngokwemvelo.
Inkomba yomkhiqizo wokuqala: amasonto angu-21. Ubudala benkukhu kusukela ekuchanyuselweni; qinisekisa uhlobo nokukhuliswa nomhlinzeki. Izinkukhu esezizozalela ziqala kamuva kulo mjikelezo.

Inkomba yokukhiqiza: 407.1–428.6 amaqanda/ngenkukhukazi efakwe endlini (hen housed), umjikelezo wokubekela kuze kube amasonto angu-90. Table 4a's cumulative 'Eggs/hen housed' for five commercial strains; the same table gives 'Age at depop. weeks 90.0' for every strain. Commercial barn/cage average, not a free-range smallholder trial. Kept as the source gives it: a per-year rate would need a point-of-lay age from another document.

Inkomba yobudala/uhlelo: SAPA 2024 commercial strain standards cumulative to 90 weeks: Dekalb Amberlink 429 eggs/hen housed, Dekalb Brown 428, Hy-Line Silver Brown 435, Hy-Line Brown 434 and Lohmann Brown Lite 413. These are full-cycle objectives, not eggs per calendar year or a smallholder forecast. Purchase age, actual onset of lay, surviving laying hens, feed, water and lighting need separate records.

Hlola izinkomba ezinemininingwane zohlobo lokukhiqiza mayelana nokudla nezindawo zokuhlala. Fanisa isabelo sokudla nendawo nesigaba sesilwane nohlelo lokuhlalisa; nikeza amanzi ahlanzekile athembekile.
In free-range systems, hens must have access to the outdoor range for at least 8 hours a day in daylight.
Where individual nest boxes are used, at least one nest for every 8 hens.
Hens need at least 8 hours of continuous darkness in every 24-hour cycle to rest properly.
Floor housing needs litter on at least a third (33%) of the floor.
The outdoor free-range area must not be overstocked: no more than 5 birds per square metre of range.
An owner or manager whose animals are, or may be, infected with a controlled animal disease must report it to the state veterinary director immediately.
Newcastle disease and notifiable avian influenza are on the state list of controlled and notifiable animal diseases.
No animal may be slaughtered anywhere but an abattoir, with the exceptions below.
Slaughter for your own household, or for cultural or religious purposes, is exempt from the abattoir rule.

animalProducts.title: Amadada: Meat duck (Pekin / Muscovy, backyard)
lines: Izakhiwo ezikhona ezingu-1; ezihlongozwayo ezingu-0. Uhlobo lokukhiqiza olukhethiwe: inyama. Akucatshangwa isibalo sezilwane noma okukhiqizwayo.
Iseluleko sokuthenga: fanisa uhlobo/izilwane nomkhiqizo, ukudla kwendawo, isimo sezulu namandla okunakekela; qinisekisa nomeluleki wendawo wemfuyo noma wokufuywa kwezinyosi.

Inkomba yomkhiqizo wokuqala: amasonto angu-7–12. P44 = Pekin (7 weeks to slaughter); MR71 = Muscovy (10 weeks for ducks/hens, 12 weeks for drakes). Treated as 'time to first product' = age to slaughter, since this is a single-cycle meat enterprise (no repeat product like eggs). Non-South-African trial by Warsaw researchers, published in SAJAS; journal location does not establish local applicability.

Inkomba yokukhiqiza: 2.3–2.9 kg yesisindo esiphilayo/ngenyoni ngesikhathi sokuhlatshwa. Non-SA (Guyana study reporting a citation to Steklenev 1990); no SA-specific absolute slaughter live-weight figure was found (see gaps). 2.93 kg = Pekin at 8-10 weeks, 2.29 kg = Muscovy at 8-10 weeks - matches this enterprise's two breeds. The same LRRD paper's own experiment (Table 2, intensive system, Guyana) measured live weight at slaughter (8 weeks) as: Pekin drakes 2.53 kg, Pekin hens 2.29 kg, Muscovy drakes 2.47 kg, Muscovy hens 1.51 kg - broadly consistent with, but not merged into, the cited range above since it is a separate dataset/table in the same source. No sourced eggs/duck/year figure was found for either breed (see gaps); the LRRD and SAJAS sources used here studied ducks reared only for meat.

Hlola izinkomba ezinemininingwane zohlobo lokukhiqiza mayelana nokudla nezindawo zokuhlala. Fanisa isabelo sokudla nendawo nesigaba sesilwane nohlelo lokuhlalisa; nikeza amanzi ahlanzekile athembekile.
It is an offence to deny a duck food or water, or keep it somewhere lacking adequate space, ventilation, light or shelter from heat and cold.
Watch flocks for sudden deaths, ruffled feathers, swollen wattles/combs or a sudden drop in egg production - these are signs of avian influenza and should be reported at once.
Keep ducks away from wild birds and open water/feed that attracts them, and control visitors' access to duck housing, to reduce avian-influenza risk.
Ducks are one of the domesticated animal species listed in the Meat Safety Act, so its rules on registered abattoirs and hygiene apply to them.
Ducks slaughtered to be sold must be slaughtered at a registered abattoir; slaughter for the farmer's own consumption is exempt but that meat may not be sold.
At the abattoir, ducks must be handled humanely during loading, transport, offloading, housing, immobilising and killing, under the Animals Protection Act.
Ducks are birds/poultry, so an outbreak of avian influenza in a duck flock is a controlled animal disease under the Animal Diseases Act and must be reported to the state vet immediately.

animalProducts.title: Ichibi elincane: Tilapia (Mozambique tilapia, small pond or tank)
lines: Izakhiwo ezikhona ezingu-1; ezihlongozwayo ezingu-0. Uhlobo lokukhiqiza olukhethiwe: inhlanzi. Akucatshangwa isibalo sezilwane noma okukhiqizwayo.
Iseluleko sokuthenga: fanisa uhlobo/izilwane nomkhiqizo, ukudla kwendawo, isimo sezulu namandla okunakekela; qinisekisa nomeluleki wendawo wemfuyo noma wokufuywa kwezinyosi.

Inkomba yomkhiqizo wokuqala: amasonto angu-43.5–52.2. 10 months x 4.35 = 43.5 weeks; 12 months x 4.35 = 52.2 weeks. This is Mozambique Tilapia (O. mossambicus) grow-out time to harvestable size; the source separately states Nile Tilapia (O. niloticus) reaches harvestable maturity faster, in 6-10 months (= 26.1-43.5 weeks) — not used here as it is a different species with a different legal status (see 'legal').

Inkomba yokukhiqiza: 800 g wesisindo ngesikhathi sokuvuna/ngenhlanzi. Table 8-3 gives the Mozambique Tilapia's harvestable size as an approximate single figure ('+- 800g'), not a range, so [800, 800] is used rather than inventing a spread. The same table cell wraps '10-12' across a line break in the PDF ('10-\n12'), kept verbatim. The table's Nile Tilapia row gives the same approximate weight (+-800g) reached faster, in 6-10 months — not used here because this dossier is framed around the indigenous, legally unrestricted Mozambique Tilapia per task instruction; see 'legal' for why Nile Tilapia is treated separately. No SA source was found giving a feed-conversion-based or per-hectare yield figure specific to O. mossambicus that could be converted to this per-fish unit without stitching numbers across documents, so outputUnit follows the source's own unit (grams harvest weight per fish) rather than being converted.

Inkomba yobudala/uhlelo: ARC makes tilapia suitability depend on water temperature: summer grow-out can be suitable anywhere in South Africa when water exceeds 20°C; growth is poor below 18°C and winter water below 13°C can kill farmed tilapia. The Highveld reference is a summer crop; tunnels can widen the range. Measure pond water and confirm stocking species and dates. Air climate or a mapped pond does not prove harvest months, fish numbers or food kg.

Hlola izinkomba ezinemininingwane zohlobo lokukhiqiza mayelana nokudla nezindawo zokuhlala. Fanisa isabelo sokudla nendawo nesigaba sesilwane nohlelo lokuhlalisa; nikeza amanzi ahlanzekile athembekile.
The indigenous Mozambique Tilapia (O. mossambicus) is not a listed invasive species and may be farmed without an alien-species permit; the faster-growing Nile Tilapia (O. niloticus) is.

Nile Tilapia (Oreochromis niloticus) is a nationally listed invasive fish species: Category 1b inside National Parks, Provincial Reserves, Mountain Catchment Areas and Forestry Reserves, and Category 3 in all other areas.
Outside protected areas Nile tilapia is Category 3: it may remain in prescribed areas or provinces, but further propagation or trade is prohibited.
Nile Tilapia has been listed under the NEMBA Alien and Invasive Species Regulations as requiring a permit to produce.
Producing an alien or invasive species (such as Nile Tilapia) is prohibited in areas designated under the Protected Areas Act and the Fish Sanctuary Act; a permit is required to produce it elsewhere.
Producing tilapia in South Africa requires a water use licence under the National Water Act.

animalProducts.title: Izimbuzi: Dairy goat (Saanen / Toggenburg / British Alpine)
lines: Izakhiwo ezikhona ezingu-1; ezihlongozwayo ezingu-0. Uhlobo lokukhiqiza olukhethiwe: ubisi. Akucatshangwa isibalo sezilwane noma okukhiqizwayo.
Iseluleko sokuthenga: fanisa uhlobo/izilwane nomkhiqizo, ukudla kwendawo, isimo sezulu namandla okunakekela; qinisekisa nomeluleki wendawo wemfuyo noma wokufuywa kwezinyosi.
Hlela ngokuzala kwangempela kwamathole/amazinyane nokuncelisa. Izilwane ezingancelisi azinikezi ubisi.
Isikhathi somkhiqizo wokuqala: asinamthombo walolu hlobo lokukhiqiza.

Inkomba yokukhiqiza: 775.4–1073.4 kg wobisi/ngembuzikazi/ngesikhathi sokuncelisa sezinsuku ezingu-305. Lowest (≥7th parity) and highest (3rd parity) group means for milk yield per 305-day standardised lactation in 16,407 analysed South African ARC Saanen lactation records, 1955–2018, mostly intensive/semi-intensive stud herds. Original PDF Table 3 labels the last group ≥7th; HTML renders it >7th. Kept in kg, without litres conversion, annualisation or yield-by-age interpolation.

Inkomba yobudala/uhlelo: South African Saanen reference by lactation number, not age in years: mean milk mass per standardised 305-day lactation was 947.3 kg at first parity, 1043.2 at second, 1073.4 at third, 1020.3 at fourth, 972.8 at fifth, 901.6 at sixth and 775.4 at ≥7th. These ARC milk-recorded groups were mostly intensive/semi-intensive stud herds. Record actual kidding date, lactation number and collected milk; do not divide these totals evenly into months.

Inkomba yobudala/uhlelo: At Putukwane near Polokwane, 179 lactating does under extensive feeding with irregular supplementation were observed for 210 days after kidding. Mean milk mass was 1.45 kg/day for Saanen, 0.75 for British Alpine and 0.56 for Toggenburg during observed lactation. Early lactation exceeded mid and late lactation; March–April kidding outperformed October–November in this cohort. These conditions differ from stud-herd records. Discuss adapted stock and feed locally; these are not litres/day or year-round promises.

Hlola izinkomba ezinemininingwane zohlobo lokukhiqiza mayelana nokudla nezindawo zokuhlala. Fanisa isabelo sokudla nendawo nesigaba sesilwane nohlelo lokuhlalisa; nikeza amanzi ahlanzekile athembekile.
It is an offence to keep a goat somewhere with inadequate space, ventilation, light or shelter from heat, cold or weather, or to confine/tether it in a way that causes unnecessary suffering.
It is an offence to starve, under-feed, or deny water or food to a goat.
An owner must not let a goat stay in a dirty or parasite-infested condition, and must get veterinary or other treatment for a sick, injured or diseased animal when able to.
Foot-and-mouth disease (FMD) is a controlled animal disease under the Animal Diseases Act: veterinary services enforce isolation and movement restrictions, and a suspected case must be reported.

Inside a declared FMD-affected zone, goats and their products (including milk) cannot be moved into, out of, or within the zone without a state veterinary movement permit and compliance with its conditions.
Every goat owner must register an official identification mark and mark their goats with it, under the Animal Identification Act.

A goat may only be slaughtered for sale at a registered abattoir under the Meat Safety Act (relevant when culled dairy does or male kids are sold for meat); slaughtering for the farmer's own consumption, or for cultural/religious purposes, is exempt but that meat may not then be sold.

animalProducts.title: Izimbuzi: Indigenous veld / communal goat (e.g. Nguni, Tankwa, Xhosa lob-ear)
lines: Izakhiwo ezikhona ezingu-1; ezihlongozwayo ezingu-0. Uhlobo lokukhiqiza olukhethiwe: inyama. Akucatshangwa isibalo sezilwane noma okukhiqizwayo.
Iseluleko sokuthenga: fanisa uhlobo/izilwane nomkhiqizo, ukudla kwendawo, isimo sezulu namandla okunakekela; qinisekisa nomeluleki wendawo wemfuyo noma wokufuywa kwezinyosi.

Inkomba yomkhiqizo wokuqala: amasonto angu-69.6–78.3. This is age at first KIDDING (birth of first kids), not first weaned kids. 16 months x 4.35 = 69.6 weeks; 18 months x 4.35 = 78.3 weeks, from doe birth to her giving birth for the first time. Adding the source's own ~150-day (~5-month, ~21.75-week) weaning assumption would put first WEANED kids at roughly 91-100 weeks of doe age, but that compound figure is not shown as the primary value since the field is documented as 'age/time from start (hatch, birth) to first product' and first kidding is the clearer, directly-stated milestone; the weaning offset is noted here for transparency.

Inkomba yobudala/uhlelo: The 2016 government goat manual distinguishes indigenous, Boer, Savanna and Kalahari Red meat-purpose stock from milk/fibre breeds, with breeding objectives and individual birth, weaning, weight and sale records. Uncontrolled communal mating can produce births at any time; that does not establish meat or weaned-kid availability all year. Choose stock for the local system and record survival and product stage before forecasting quantities.

Inkomba yobudala/uhlelo: In KZN Highland Sourveld smallholder systems, winter and early-spring feed shortage can restrict goats. Autumn-kidding does feed kids through winter; spring-kidding does face late-pregnancy feed shortage, especially with late rains. Plan local winter feed and monitor weights with extension support; this is regional care context, not kg or a universal kidding calendar.

Hlola izinkomba ezinemininingwane zohlobo lokukhiqiza mayelana nokudla nezindawo zokuhlala. Fanisa isabelo sokudla nendawo nesigaba sesilwane nohlelo lokuhlalisa; nikeza amanzi ahlanzekile athembekile.
It is an offence to keep a goat somewhere with inadequate space, ventilation, light or shelter from heat, cold or weather, or to confine/tether it in a way that causes unnecessary suffering.
It is an offence to starve, under-feed, or deny water or food to a goat.
An owner must not let a goat stay in a dirty or parasite-infested condition, and must get veterinary or other treatment for a sick, injured or diseased animal when able to.

Winter feed shortage on communal sourveld is a known welfare/production risk: does that kid in autumn must feed kids through winter, and does that kid in spring suffer poor nutrition during late pregnancy, so winter feed supplementation matters.
Foot-and-mouth disease (FMD) is a controlled animal disease under the Animal Diseases Act: veterinary services enforce isolation and movement restrictions, and a suspected case must be reported.
Inside a declared FMD-affected zone, goats and their products cannot be moved into, out of, or within the zone without a state veterinary movement permit and compliance with its conditions.
Every goat owner, including communal/smallholder owners, must register an official identification mark and mark their goats with it, under the Animal Identification Act.

A goat may only be slaughtered for sale at a registered abattoir under the Meat Safety Act; slaughtering it for the farmer's own consumption, or for cultural/religious purposes (including ceremonial slaughter, common with indigenous goats), is exempt from that rule, but that meat may not then be sold.

lay, surviving laying hens, feed, water and lighting need separate records.

In free-range systems, hens must have access to the outdoor range for at least 8 hours a day in daylight.

Hens need at least 8 hours of continuous darkness in every 24-hour cycle to rest properly.
Floor housing needs litter on at least a third (33%) of the floor.
The outdoor free-range area must not be overstocked: no more than 5 birds per square metre of range.
An owner or manager whose animals are, or may be, infected with a controlled animal disease must report it to the
state veterinary director immediately.
Newcastle disease and notifiable avian influenza are on the state list of controlled and notifiable animal diseases.
No animal may be slaughtered anywhere but an abattoir, with the exceptions below.
Slaughter for your own household, or for cultural or religious purposes, is exempt from the abattoir rule.

Izakhiwo ezikhona ezingu-1; ezihlongozwayo ezingu-0. Uhlobo lokukhiqiza olukhethiwe: inyama. Akucatshangwa
isibalo sezilwane noma okukhiqizwayo.
Iseluleko sokuthenga: fanisa uhlobo/izilwane nomkhiqizo, ukudla kwendawo, isimo sezulu namandla okunakekela;
qinisekisa nomeluleki wendawo wemfuyo noma wokufuywa kwezinyosi.
Inkomba yomkhiqizo wokuqala: amasonto angu-69.6–78.3. This is age at first KIDDING (birth of first kids), not first
weaned kids. 16 months x 4.35 = 69.6 weeks; 18 months x 4.35 = 78.3 weeks, from doe birth to her giving birth for
the first time. Adding the source's own ~150-day (~5-month, ~21.75-week) weaning assumption would put first
WEANED kids at roughly 91-100 weeks of doe age, but that compound figure is not shown as the primary value
since the field is documented as 'age/time from start (hatch, birth) to first product' and first kidding is the clearer,
directly-stated milestone; the weaning offset is noted here for transparency.
Inkomba yobudala/uhlelo: The 2016 government goat manual distinguishes indigenous, Boer, Savanna and
Kalahari Red meat-purpose stock from milk/fibre breeds, with breeding objectives and individual birth, weaning,
weight and sale records. Uncontrolled communal mating can produce births at any time; that does not establish
meat or weaned-kid availability all year. Choose stock for the local system and record survival and product stage
before forecasting quantities.
Inkomba yobudala/uhlelo: In KZN Highland Sourveld smallholder systems, winter and early-spring feed shortage
can restrict goats. Autumn-kidding does feed kids through winter; spring-kidding does face late-pregnancy feed
shortage, especially with late rains. Plan local winter feed and monitor weights with extension support; this is
regional care context, not kg or a universal kidding calendar.
Hlola izinkomba ezinemininingwane zohlobo lokukhiqiza mayelana nokudla nezindawo zokuhlala. Fanisa isabelo
sokudla nendawo nesigaba sesilwane nohlelo lokuhlalisa; nikeza amanzi ahlanzekile athembekile.
It is an offence to keep a goat somewhere with inadequate space, ventilation, light or shelter from heat, cold or
weather, or to confine/tether it in a way that causes unnecessary suffering.
It is an offence to starve, under-feed, or deny water or food to a goat.
An owner must not let a goat stay in a dirty or parasite-infested condition, and must get veterinary or other
treatment for a sick, injured or diseased animal when able to.
Winter feed shortage on communal sourveld is a known welfare/production risk: does that kid in autumn must
feed kids through winter, and does that kid in spring suffer poor nutrition during late pregnancy, so winter feed
supplementation matters.
Foot-and-mouth disease (FMD) is a controlled animal disease under the Animal Diseases Act: veterinary services
enforce isolation and movement restrictions, and a suspected case must be reported.
Inside a declared FMD-affected zone, goats and their products cannot be moved into, out of, or within the zone
without a state veterinary movement permit and compliance with its conditions.
Every goat owner, including communal/smallholder owners, must register an official identification mark and mark
their goats with it, under the Animal Identification Act.
A goat may only be slaughtered for sale at a registered abattoir under the Meat Safety Act; slaughtering it for the
farmer's own consumption, or for cultural/religious purposes (including ceremonial slaughter, common with
indigenous goats), is exempt from that rule, but that meat may not then be sold.
